newsitem.title: FRANCE: Peugeot denies told to delay layoffs announcement.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot denies told to delay layoffs announcement.

text.p: Car-maker Peugeot denied on Saturday that it had been asked by the French government to delay the announcement of a layoff plan because of a furore over Renault's closure of a Belgian plant.
But a Peugeot spokeswoman would not confirm nor deny that it was considering laying off close to 1,300 people as reported by French weekly Gestion Sociale on Friday.
The magazine said the plan had been submitted by Peugeot chairman Jacques Calvet to the Labour Ministry, and that Calvet had been asked to delay publication of the Renault controversy.
"It's incorrect that we were asked to delay the announcement of a labour plan. There is no labour plan to announce for the time being," the spokeswoman said.
"All there is now is discussion with competent authorities on staff adjustments which will unfortunately have to be made," she said.

But she said she did not know whether 1,300 layoffs were being envisaged. The current labour plan for Peugeot, which runs out in June, provided for 1,260 layoffs and the spokeswoman said there would be no change in the pace of layoffs in the next plan.
A spokesman for the Labour Ministry also denied a plan had been submitted.

Renault workers staged brief strikes in several countries on Friday as the fallout over plans to close the large Belgian plant of Vilvoorde with the loss of 3,100 jobs spread, while Spain halted subsidies to the company.
